title: My Country 'Tis of Thee
description: My Country 'Tis of Thee in Tonic Solfa to DORT, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Samuel Francis Smith wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 836 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “National Hymn”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Sixes and Fours (6.6.4.6.6.6.4), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to DORT; any other Sixes and Fours tune fits them as well.
underlay: My coun-try 'tis of thee, Sweet land of lib-er-ty, Of thee I sing; Land where my fa-thers died, Land of the pil-grim's pride, From ev-ery moun-tain side Let free-dom ring.

lines: I love thy rocks and rills,
And ring from all the trees
Long may our land be bright

licence: Public domain: Samuel Francis Smith died in 1895.
credits: Words by Samuel Francis Smith (1808–1895), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to DORT by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
